interpretive_safeguards.dining_separation: Genesis 43:32 is treated as debated social-boundary language; historical corroboration is limited and it is not mapped to modern racial categories.
interpretive_safeguards.divination_cup: Genesis 44’s steward allegation and Egyptian divination comparison do not prove Joseph personally practiced pagan divination; court persona/ruse/actual context remain open readings.
interpretive_safeguards.egyptian_court_and_dreams: Court offices are translated cautiously; dream practices are comparative context while Joseph attributes interpretation to God in the narrative.
interpretive_safeguards.egyptian_names_on: Zaphenath-paneah’s Egyptian etymology remains uncertain; On is conventionally identified with Heliopolis, without identifying Asenath or Potiphera historically.
interpretive_safeguards.garment: Genesis 37:3’s garment may be ornamented, long-sleeved, multicolored, or a special tunic/status garment; no single rendering is certain.
interpretive_safeguards.ishmaelite_midianite: Recognizes a real literary/textual complexity, presents debated serious explanations, rejects invented nested-caravan harmonization, and does not call the text necessarily contradictory.
interpretive_safeguards.joseph_potiphar: Joseph is an enslaved foreigner under household power; refusal, trust, accusation, and custody are treated without romanticizing. Potiphar is not historically identified.
interpretive_safeguards.judah_arc_and_substitution: Judah’s Genesis 37, 38, 43, and 44 acts form a developing narrative arc. Offering himself for Benjamin is immediate narrative action; later Christian typology is reception context.
interpretive_safeguards.judah_tamar_levirate: Genesis 38 is integral; the kinship duty predates Deuteronomy 25 and is not simply an application of that later law. Onan’s refusal is not reduced to masturbation.
interpretive_safeguards.pharaoh_administration_chronology: No certain Pharaoh, named Joseph identification, specific dynasty, or archaeological proof of the seven-year famine is claimed. The one-fifth and storage plan is not treated as a complete Egyptian tax record.
interpretive_safeguards.slave_price: Twenty shekels is narrated; it does not prove an exact patriarchal date.
interpretive_safeguards.testing_recognition: The spy accusation is a narrative test, not assumed standard Egyptian law; the recognition asymmetry is not given one certain cause; the interpreter and returned silver remain in view.
interpretive_safeguards.zonah_qedeshah: Distinguishes prostitution-related zonah/qedeshah usage from later institutional sacred-prostitution claims, whose historiography is disputed.
